SECTION 01 THEORETICAL SPECIFICATION

1. Theoretical Foundations of Relational Division ($R \div S$)

In Relational Algebra, Relational Division ($R \div S$) is the algebraic counterpart of the universal quantifier ($\forall$) in first-order predicate logic. While projection ($\Pi$) reduces dimensions, selection ($\sigma$) filters rows, and Cartesian product ($\times$) generates all combinatorial pairs, relational division identifies candidate entities in a dividend relation $R$ that are associated with every single requirement listed in a divisor relation $S$.

FORMAL PREDICATE LOGIC DEFINITION:
$$R \div S = \{ t_A \in \Pi_A(R) \mid \forall t_B \in S, \langle t_A, t_B \rangle \in R \}$$
Schema Requirements: $\text{attr}(R) = A \cup B$, $\text{attr}(S) = B$, where $A \cap B = \emptyset$, and $A = \text{attr}(R) - \text{attr}(S) \neq \emptyset$. The result schema is strictly $A$.

Equivalence in First-Order Logic (Universal Negation & De Morgan):

Because first-order predicate logic satisfies the De Morgan equivalence for quantifiers:

$$\forall y \in S [ P(x, y) ] \iff \neg \exists y \in S [ \neg P(x, y) ]$$

An entity $x$ qualifies for $R \div S$ if and only if there does NOT exist any item $y \in S$ for which the entity $x$ fails to have record $\langle x, y \rangle$ in $R$. This fundamental theorem forms the exact mathematical foundation for correlated SQL subqueries.

SECTION 02 ALGEBRAIC DERIVATION

2. The 5-Step Relational Algebra Pipeline

Relational division is a derived operator rather than a primitive operator in Codd's foundational algebra. It is algebraically synthesized using five fundamental primitive operations ($\Pi, \times, -$):

$$R \div S = \Pi_A(R) - \Pi_A( (\Pi_A(R) \times S) - R )$$
T1

Candidate Projection: $T_1 = \Pi_A(R)$

Projects relation $R$ onto candidate attribute set $A$, isolating all unique candidate entities eligible for qualification.

T2

Theoretical Cartesian Pairings: $T_2 = T_1 \times S$

Pairs every candidate entity with every requirement present in divisor relation $S$ (the total combinatorial required matrix).

T3

Disqualifying Missing Pairs: $T_3 = T_2 - R$

Set difference isolating requirement pairings that candidates should possess but are missing from actual records in $R$.

T4

Disqualified Entities: $T_4 = \Pi_A(T_3)$

Projects candidate entities that failed at least one requirement in $S$ (unfulfilled candidates).

T5

Final Qualified Result: $T_5 = T_1 - T_4 = R \div S$

Subtracts disqualified entities from the candidate universe, leaving only entities that satisfied 100% of divisor criteria.

SECTION 03 SQL ENGINE

3. Multi-Paradigm SQL Compilation

Standard ANSI/ISO SQL (ISO/IEC 9075) lacks a native DIVIDE BY keyword. The simulator dynamically compiles queries into three canonical paradigms:

1. Correlated Double NOT EXISTS

Universal Portability

Directly encodes the logical identity $\neg \exists y \in S [\neg P(x, y)]$. Candidate $x$ qualifies if there is no requirement $y$ in $S$ that $x$ lacks in $R$. Universally portable across PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, and SQLite.

2. Aggregation (GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT)

Optimized HashAgg

Joins $R$ and $S$ on divisor attributes, groups tuples by candidate identity, and asserts: HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT R.item) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM S). Highly favored in production relational database query planners for high-throughput analytics.

3. Set Difference (EXCEPT / MINUS)

Pure Relational

Evaluates whether $(S - \text{Items possessed by Candidate } x) = \emptyset$. Supported natively in PostgreSQL, SQLite, and SQL Server (via EXCEPT) and Oracle (via MINUS).

SECTION 04 ESP32 / MPU-6050

4. Embedded Hardware & Sensor Telemetry Coupling

To fulfill the experiential Activity-Based Learning mandate, the platform bridges relational query processing with real-time embedded telemetry from an ESP32 microcontroller interfacing an MPU-6050 6-DOF Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) over I2C (Address 0x68).

• High-Frequency Sampling: Continuous 50Hz ingestion of 3-axis accelerometer ($a_x, a_y, a_z$) and 3-axis gyroscope ($\omega_x, \omega_y, \omega_z$) frames.
• Kinematics Pipeline: Live calculation of Pitch, Roll, and Yaw angles through complementary sensor filtering.
• Query Execution Concurrency: Synchronous benchmarking of relational division operations (1,400+ ops/sec) alongside active sensor ingestion and comparison metrics.

SECTION 08 OPERATIONAL MANUAL

8. Operational User Manual & Step-by-Step Guide

Follow these instructions to configure inputs, execute the algebraic pipeline, inspect intermediate data structures, and export academic reports:

Step 1: Domain Scenario Preset Selection

Open the simulation workspace and navigate to the Active Domain Scenario dropdown in the left control sidebar, or use the Quick Jump Matrix on the Dashboard. Select one of the six pre-configured industry benchmarks (e.g. 01: University CS Core Courses, 02: Cloud DevOps & SRE Stack, or 06: Project Apollo Space Crew). The tables for Dividend Relation $R$ and Divisor Relation $S$ will instantly populate.

Step 2: Relation Schema & Tuple Editing

Click any cell directly in Table $R$ or Table $S$ to edit candidate names or required attributes inline. Use the + button to append tuples, or click the red ✕ icon to delete unwanted records. Click the CSV button to download raw tabular data.

Step 3: Tactile Hardware Controls (Exact & Fuzzy Modes)

Toggle Exact Division ($R \div_{\text{exact}} S$) if you wish to enforce strict equality (candidates possessing extra items outside $S$ are disqualified). Alternatively, adjust the Fuzzy Match Threshold slider (0% to 100%) to accept partial candidates meeting an academic cutoff.

Step 4: Pipeline Execution & Hotkey

Click the prominent blue ▶ Execute Relational Pipeline button in the left panel, or press the universal shortcut Cmd/Ctrl + Enter. The execution engine will evaluate intermediate states in under 1 millisecond.

Step 5: Multi-Pane Inspection & Deep Debugging

Use the central tab buttons to navigate the computed data structures:
  • Output Result ($T_5$): Final qualified candidates satisfying universal quantification.
  • Operator DAG Tree: Interactive Abstract Syntax Tree showing algebraic operators with clickable node inspection.
  • 5-Step Derivation: Side-by-side display of $T_1$, $T_2$, $T_3$, and $T_4$ intermediate relations.
  • Tuple Tracer: Interactive step-debugger checking the condition $\forall y \in S, \langle x, y \rangle \in R$ per candidate.
  • SQL Studio: Synthesized Double NOT EXISTS, Aggregation, and EXCEPT queries.
  • ESP32 Telemetry: Live 50Hz IMU sensor metrics and database engine comparison frequency.
  • Test Suite: 8-case automated boundary verification runner.

Step 6: Report Generation & Multi-Format Downloads

Click the ⬇ Export button in the top navigation bar or press Alt + E. Select from PDF Academic Report, Word (.doc), Plain Text (.txt), or CSV Datasets to download your verified execution logs.
